messages:
incident-bot: Paging: P99 routing tail latency SLO breach detected in eu-west-2 (automated alert). Severity P2. Metric: router.request_latency.p99 >= 300ms for 3m. Streaming stalls observed on streaming-proxy in same region. Incident created: INC-1729991111 :rotating_light:

meera: on it. sam oncall? can you pick this up and confirm customer impact? mention if this is related to the recent routing policy rollout.

sam: I'm the oncall, taking lead. pulling metrics now.

sam: quick snapshot from grafana (last 5m):
```
region eu-west-2: p95=185ms (SLO=150ms), p99=435ms (SLO=300ms)
streaming_proxy.stalls=24 (baseline ~2)
inflight requests queue depth +42% on router-hosts
```

sam: paging pgd oncall and sieving logs. @jordan any recent policy changes to routing in eu-west-2?

jordan: yes, we started a staged rollout of router-weight policy v2 at 1729989000. Stage 3 targeted eu-west-2. I flagged it as low-risk but there was an experimental hot-lane heuristic enabled (hotlane=true).

aj: heatmap from shard analyzer -> `hotkey_shard_breakdown` shows shard-42 is getting 58% of traffic in eu-west-2 (normally ~5-7%). suspect hot partition + policy change amplifying it.

meera: that explains tail. if traffic concentrates on shard-42 some hosts get saturated and kv cache thrash. can we roll back the policy to v1 for eu-west-2 only?

sam: prepping rollback. infra runbook suggests `rollback-routing-policy` for partial rollbacks.

sam: running command now:
```
# partial rollback to v1 for eu-west-2
deployctl routing rollback --policy router-weight-v1 --region eu-west-2 --reason "p99 spike"
```

infra-bot: deployctl: rollback started (id: rb-1729991123). Applying config to eu-west-2 control-plane. ETA ~45s. :gear:

sam: rollback applied. infra-bot confirms config version now router-weight-v1.

infra-bot: config change logged: rb-1729991123 by sam. No pod restarts required.

sam: re-checking metrics. p99 dropped from 435ms -> 312ms in 60s, p95 -> 160ms. streaming stalls down to 8. still above SLO but improving.

support-eng: customer impact: support tickets showing 12 affected customers during window, two customers reported visible streaming reconnections, one enterprise reported intermittent 5xx for 30-90s. tagging CS to send notice.

meera: good mitigation. next steps: 1) keep rollback in place for 30m monitoring, 2) isolate hot partition traffic pattern (who is spiking shard-42), 3) plan root cause and follow-up fix (policy tweak to ignore hot keys or backpressure).

jordan: I will open a follow-up RFC to change hotlane heuristic to include per-shard cap and more conservative rollout gating.

aj: running a TTL eviction for shard-42 cache to reduce thrash and temp throttle heavy keys. command: `kvctl evict --shard shard-42 --ttl 30s`. executed.

sam: metrics now: p99=278ms, p95=150ms, streaming stalls=3. Looks back within SLO for p95, p99 still marginal but trending down.

meera: thanks. please update PagerDuty incident status and assign the postmortem to jordan + sam + aj. include impact timeline and customer list. support-eng, can you draft customer advisory? keep it short and actionable.

support-eng: drafting customer message: "We experienced elevated latency and streaming interruptions in eu-west-2 from 12:04–12:11 UTC due to a routing policy change that concentrated traffic on a shard. We rolled back the policy and applied mitigations; normal service restored by 12:14 UTC. If you saw reconnects or errors, please reply and we'll prioritize follow-up." will send after review.

meera: final ask: record all commands and screenshots in the incident doc. schedule 1h scrub with affected teams in 24h. great job triaging quickly. :thumbsup:

sam: leaving oncall note and transitioning to secondary. handing off to aj for monitoring for next 30m.

aj: ack. will watch dashboards and escalate back if anything flares.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1729991111 updated: severity P2 -> monitoring, timeline recorded, assigned to jordan for follow-up.

support-eng: customer advisory queued to send in 10m.

meera: closing here for now, will convert to postmortem when the ticket is created. thanks everyone. :pray:
